title: The enterprise guide to securing coding agents
summary: Anthropic published a guide for security and technical leaders on securing Claude Code on Team and Enterprise plans, covering six evaluation questions, four risks (credential leakage, unvetted dependencies, data exfiltration, and prompt injection), and layered controls such as sandboxing, permission rules, and managed settings. Auto mode is now the default starting mode for interactive Claude Code sessions on all plans, while headless, Agent SDK, and HIPAA setups default to manual, and Enterprise plans gained scanning of skills and plugins for malicious content. The guide recommends piloting on a low-sensitivity repo before expanding.

title: Linked billing on the Claude Platform
summary: In beta, third-party platforms can bill customers' Claude API usage without sharing an API key. Customers link their Claude Platform org, approve each platform, set a spend limit, and can unlink at any time, while platforms no longer need to store or rotate keys or build their own metering, and can choose per request who pays. The caveat is that requests run in the platform's org, so customer IP allowlists, encryption keys, and retention settings do not apply.

title: Zero data retention with Enterprise Frontier Safeguards is now in beta
summary: Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS) detects sophisticated misuse while keeping zero data retention intact, and has moved from a private beta with 100+ customers to a public beta where eligible customers can get setup instructions. It monitors misuse patterns across many requests and creates Safety Cases for review that exclude inputs and outputs, with analysis running on data in the customer's cloud storage. It works on Claude Platform, Claude Platform on AWS, Bedrock, and Claude on Google Cloud, with Microsoft Foundry coming soon, helping regulated and security-sensitive organizations keep data custody.

title: KPMG's Todd Lohr on AI when your data is also your clients' data
summary: In an interview, KPMG US Vice Chair Todd Lohr explains how KPMG integrated Claude into its Digital Gateway tax platform while protecting client data. KPMG had early access to Enterprise Frontier Safeguards, now in public beta and compatible with zero data retention, which lets regulated firms keep client data in infrastructure they control while using frontier models. Lohr argues that firms must adopt and secure AI simultaneously, since "wait and see" is unsustainable.

title: MCP servers can now ship skills, run tasks, and more with Claude
summary: MCP now lets servers work with Claude more like another agent, with Skills over MCP in public beta so servers can bundle guidance with their tools, loaded on demand and updated with the server. Tasks (background long-running jobs) and Elicitation (pausing to ask the user for input) are now generally available. File Uploads is rolling out soon so PDFs, spreadsheets, and images can reach servers without using the context window, and the update is part of an open spec that other compatible clients can use.

title: Turn artifacts into Mac and Windows apps
summary: The beta Install as app option turns Claude artifacts into desktop apps with their own icon and window that open outside Claude and can be shared, with no API key or separate login needed. Access is permission-based, ranging from browser-level permissions to app features like notifications and menu bar to full computer access, and apps auto-update when the artifact is edited with permissions re-requested after updates. Apps are not reviewed by Anthropic, usage counts toward plan limits, and the feature is unavailable to HIPAA-ready organizations and hybrid deployments.
